name: the-harness-collapses-and-drags-on-request
description:
Graded on the harness itself. A drag asks for a width and is graded on the width the window printed, correcting itself when the synthetic gesture lands short. A collapse lands after that drag - the case the chord drops - through the chrome row's own toggle rather than the keyboard. And an eval polls until the page's animation-only width clears instead of sampling it mid-motion.

The two waits at the end are the same assertion made two ways: the collapse is graded on the window's own request line and on the pixels the rows stood in.

actions.note: The grip sits at the sidebar's right edge, 280 wide in this fixture. Asked for 360, and graded on what the window printed.
Polled, not sampled. The page holds a width only while the pane animates, and a sample taken during the drag's own animation reads 'held' - which is the reading that used to look like a finding.
After a drag, which is the case the chord drops

assertions.desc: The polled eval settled once the animation ended.

assertions.pattern: Atrium: sidebar toggle requested from the chrome row
assertions.label: the-collapse-landed
assertions.desc: The toggle ran after a drag, where the chord used to go nowhere.
In pixels: the rows' column now shows the page card.
